requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: General or particular encoding rules CAN be specified by `encode` and `variant` attributes.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, general or particular encoding rules can be specified by using encode and variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A `variant` attribute IS a reference to a specific encoding variant.
requirements.original: Variant attributes allow references to specific encoding variants.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute IS denoted by the keyword `variant` in a with statement.
requirements.original: variant

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: a refinement, not a replacement, of the current encoding scheme is to be specified
requirements.canonical: A `variant` attribute SHALL be used to specify a refinement of the currently specified encoding scheme instead of its replacement.
requirements.original: To specify a refinement of the currently specified encoding scheme instead of its replacement, the variant attribute shall be used.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A `variant` attribute IS closely related to `encode` attributes and therefore differs from other attributes.
requirements.original: The variant attributes are different from other attributes, because they are closely related to encode attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: Additional overwriting rules defined in clause 27.1.2.1 apply to `variant` attributes.
requirements.original: Therefore, for variant attributes, additional overwriting rules apply (see clause 27.1.2.1).

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for simple basic types IS given in list items a) to e) of clause 27.5 ("8 bit" ... "IEEE754 extended double").
requirements.original: The following strings are the predefined (standardized) variant attributes for simple basic types (see clause E.2.1):

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "8 bit" or "unsigned 8 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "8 bit" or "unsigned 8 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 8 bits (single byte) within the system.
requirements.original: a) "8 bit" and "unsigned 8 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 8-bits (single byte) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "16 bit" or "unsigned 16 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "16 bit" or "unsigned 16 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 16 bits (two bytes) within the system.
requirements.original: b) "16 bit" and "unsigned 16 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 16-bits (two bytes) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "32 bit" or "unsigned 32 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "32 bit" or "unsigned 32 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 32 bits (four bytes) within the system.
requirements.original: c) "32 bit" and "unsigned 32 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 32-bits (four bytes) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "64 bit" or "unsigned 64 bit" applied to an integer or enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "64 bit" or "unsigned 64 bit" is applied to an integer or enumerated type, the integer value or the integer numbers associated with the enumerated values SHALL be handled as represented on 64 bits (eight bytes) within the system.
requirements.original: d) "64 bit" and "unsigned 64 bit" mean, when applied to integer and enumerated types, that the integer value or the integer numbers associated with enumerated values shall be handled as it was represented on 64-bits (eight bytes) within the system.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: an IEEE754 variant is applied to a float type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "IEEE754 float", "IEEE754 double", "IEEE754 extended float" or "IEEE754 extended double" is applied to a float type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to IEEE 754.
requirements.original: e) "IEEE754 float","IEEE754 double", "IEEE754 extended float" and "IEEE754 extended double" mean, when applied to a float type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the standard IEEE 754 [6] (see annex E).

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for charstring and universal charstring types IS given in list items a) to h) following this sentence ("UTF-8" ... "8 bit").
requirements.original: The following strings are the predefined (standardized) variant attributes for charstring and `universal` charstring (see clause E.2.2):

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-8" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-8" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-8 as defined in clause 10.1 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: a) "UTF-8" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-8 as defined in clause 10.1 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-16" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-16" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16 as defined in clause 10.4 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: b) "UTF-16" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16 as defined in clause 10.4 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-16LE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-16LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16LE as defined in clause 10.3 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: c) "UTF-16LE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that each character of the value shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-16LE as defined in clause 10.3 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

ambiguity.issue: Only "UTF-16LE" (and the charstring "8 bit") prescribes individual encoding of each character; all other UTF variants encode "the value". It is unclear whether the difference is intended. Chose the literal wording.
readings: When the variant attribute "UTF-16LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to UTF-16LE.
When the variant attribute "UTF-16LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value as a whole SHALL be encoded and decoded according to UTF-16LE, like the other UTF variants.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-16BE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-16BE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-16BE as defined in clause 10.2 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: d) "UTF-16BE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-16BE as defined in clause 10.2 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-32" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-32" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32 as defined in clause 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: e) "UTF-32" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-32 as defined in clause 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-32LE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-32LE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32LE as defined in clause 10.6 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: f) "UTF-32LE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-32LE as defined in clause 10.6 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "UTF-32BE" applied to a universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "UTF-32BE" is applied to a universal charstring type, the value SHALL be encoded and decoded according to the UCS encoding scheme UTF-32BE as defined in clause 10.5 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: g) "UTF-32BE" means, when applied to the universal charstring type, that the value shall be encoded and decoded according to the UCS Encoding scheme UTF-32BE as defined in clause 10.5 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "8 bit" applied to a charstring or universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "8 bit" is applied to a charstring or universal charstring type, each character of the value SHALL be individually encoded and decoded according to the 8-bit coded representation specified in ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: h) "8 bit" means, when applied to charstring and universal charstring types, that each character of the value shall be individually encoded and decoded according to the coded representation as specified in ISO/IEC 10646 [2] (an 8-bit coding).

requirements.subject: ent:ucs-encoding-scheme
requirements.canonical: A UCS encoding scheme permits an optional signature (byte order mark, BOM) to be present in encoded character strings.
requirements.original: NOTE: The UCS Encoding schemes allow an optional signature (also known as Byte Order Mark, BOM) to be present in encoded character strings.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A UCS encoding scheme variant attribute IS NOT specifying whether signatures (BOM) are present in the encoded value; the presence of signatures is an option of the encoder.
requirements.original: The above UCS encoding scheme variant attributes does not specify, if signatures are present in the encoded values or not, this is an option for the encoder.

ambiguity.issue: "does not specify, if signatures are present" uses the plural verb mismatch and "signatures" for BOM; meaning is clear.

requirements.subject: ent:decoder
requirements.canonical: A decoder SHOULD be able to process signatures (BOM) in the decoding process.
requirements.original: It is expected that decoders are able to process signatures in the decoding process.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The set of predefined (standardized) variant attributes for structured types IS given in list item a) following this sentence ("IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6").
requirements.original: The following strings are the predefined (standardized) variant attributes for structured types (see clause E.2.2.4):

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant "IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6" applied to a record type
requirements.canonical: When the variant attribute "IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6" is applied to a record type, the value SHALL be handled as an IDL fixed point decimal value.
requirements.original: a) "IDL:fixed FORMAL/01-12-01 v.2.6" means, when applied to a record type, that the value shall be handled as an IDL fixed point decimal value (see annex E).

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A predefined variant attribute MAY be used in combination with a more general encode attribute specified at a higher level.
requirements.original: These variant attributes can be used in combination with the more general encode attributes specified at a higher level.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: UTF-8 variant on a universal charstring inside a module with global encode "BER:1997"
requirements.canonical: When a universal charstring has the variant attribute "UTF-8" within a module that has the global encode attribute "BER:1997", each character of the string value IS first encoded following the UTF-8 rules and the resulting UTF-8 value IS then encoded following the BER rules.
requirements.original: For example a universal charstring specified with the variant attribute "UTF-8" within a module which itself has a global encoding attribute "BER:1997" (see clause 12.2 of ETSI ES 201 873-7 [i.5]) will cause each character of the values within the string to first be encoded following the UTF-8 rules and then this UTF-8 value will be encoded following the more global BER rules.

requirements.subject: ent:invalid-encoding-rule
requirements.condition: invalid encoding rules are to be specified
requirements.canonical: An invalid encoding rule SHALL be specified in a referenceable source external to the module in the same way as valid encoding rules are referenced.
requirements.original: If it is desired to specify invalid encoding rules then these shall be specified in a referenceable source external to the module in the same way that valid encoding rules are referenced.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: multiple encodings (clause 27.4) are used
requirements.canonical: If multiple encodings are used, the value of a variant attribute SHALL be composed of two parts separated by a dot.
requirements.original: If multiple encodings (see clause 27.4) are used, the variant attribute value shall be composed of two parts separated by a dot.

ambiguity.issue: "If multiple encodings are used" does not say where they are used. Chose: multiple encode attributes are associated with the element that the variant applies to.
readings: If multiple encode attributes are associated with the element a variant attribute applies to, the value of that variant attribute SHALL be composed of two parts separated by a dot.
If multiple encodings are used anywhere in the module, the value of every variant attribute SHALL be composed of two parts separated by a dot.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: A variant attribute whose value is composed of an encoding reference and a variant value separated by a dot IS called an encoding related variant attribute.
requirements.original: Such variant attributes are called encoding related variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The first part (before the dot) of an encoding related variant attribute IS the specification of the encodings the variant is related to.
requirements.original: The first part of the attribute specifies the encodings the variant is related to.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant related to a single encoding
requirements.canonical: When the variant is related to a single encode attribute, the first part of an encoding related variant attribute IS a simple string.
requirements.original: There are two possible notations: either a simple string when the variant is related to a single encode attribute or a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets if the variant is related to multiple encodings.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.condition: variant related to multiple encodings
requirements.canonical: When the variant is related to multiple encodings, the first part of an encoding related variant attribute IS a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets.
requirements.original: There are two possible notations: either a simple string when the variant is related to a single encode attribute or a comma separated list of strings enclosed in curly brackets if the variant is related to multiple encodings.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The second part (following the dot) of an encoding related variant attribute IS a simple string that specifies the variant value.
requirements.original: The second part of the attribute (following the dot symbol) is a simple string that specifies the variant value.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encoding related variant attribute IS valid only when the related encoding is selected.
requirements.original: The encoding related attributes are valid only when the related encoding is selected.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.condition: multiple encodings are used
requirements.canonical: If multiple encodings are used, a variant attribute SHALL NOT be defined without an encoding reference.
requirements.original: It is not allowed to define variant attributes with no encoding reference if multiple encodings are used.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A with statement MAY contain any number of variant attributes.
requirements.original: The with statement can contain any number of variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-related-variant-attribute
requirements.condition: dot notation is used in the variant attribute value
requirements.canonical: When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot SHALL resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.
requirements.original: a) When dot notation is used in the variant attribute value for an element, the strings preceding the dot symbol shall resolve into one of the encode attribute values associated with the same element.

non_requirement.reason: introductory sentence of the restrictions list; general static rules of clause 5 apply
